must_teach: In the pre-active (planning) phase decisions are calm and rational; in the interactive phase the teacher must respond at once to learners' cues with little time to deliberate, so decisions are spontaneous.

concept: Features of seminar, symposium, workshop, conference
must_teach: A seminar has a chairperson, paper presenter(s) and participants; a symposium has prepared talks and normally ends with audience questions; a workshop stresses hands-on practical work; a conference covers a broad theme through several sessions.

concept: Morrison's mastery formula
must_teach: Morrison's mastery formula: pre-test, teach, test the result, adapt procedure, teach and test again to the point of actual learning. Non-mastery signals a change of teaching procedure, not simple repetition or moving on.

concept: Sternberg's triarchic theory: analytical, creative, practical
must_teach: Sternberg's triarchic theory: analytical (componential) for academic problems, creative (experiential) for novelty, practical (contextual) for adapting to, shaping and selecting everyday environments ('street smarts'). Crystallised intelligence is Cattell's.

concept: Relative grading drawback in small uniformly able class
must_teach: Relative grading distributes grades by position in the group, so in a small, uniformly able class some good performers must receive low grades; absolute grading uses fixed standards and avoids this.

concept: Seating arrangement and the classroom action zone
must_teach: Seating affects interaction: students in the front and centre ('action zone') interact most with the teacher, and circular seating increases student-to-student talk; back-row students do not participate more.

concept: SWAYAM features: free learning, fee-based proctored exam, access-equity-quality
must_teach: SWAYAM courses are free to study by any learner anywhere; certification requires a fee-based proctored examination; it is designed around the three cardinal principles of access, equity and quality. It is not restricted to IIT students.

concept: Direction of reasoning in inductive, deductive, analytic, synthetic methods
must_teach: Induction: particular to general; deduction: general to particular; analysis: unknown to known (from what is to be found back to data); synthesis: known to unknown.

concept: Acceleration vs enrichment for gifted learners
must_teach: Acceleration moves gifted learners faster through the curriculum (grade skipping, early entry, advanced courses); enrichment adds depth and breadth at the same grade; ability grouping places similar-ability learners together; remediation corrects deficiencies.

concept: Ausubel's three conditions for meaningful learning
must_teach: Ausubel's conditions: logically meaningful material, relevant anchoring ideas in cognitive structure, and a meaningful learning set (intention to relate new to known). Intending only verbatim memorising makes learning rote; reception (lecture) learning can be meaningful.

concept: Limitations of true-false, matching, essay and MCQ items
must_teach: True-false items allow a 50 per cent chance by guessing; matching items suit only homogeneous associations; essay scoring varies between examiners (subjectivity); MCQs need plausible distractors that are hard to write.

concept: Lack of laboratory affects psychomotor objectives most
must_teach: Laboratories provide handling of apparatus, measuring and observing, so their absence prevents psychomotor (manipulative skill) objectives; cognitive knowledge can still be partly gained from lectures. Instructional facilities limit achievable objectives.

concept: Expectancy-value theory: motivation as product of expectancy and value
must_teach: Expectancy-value theory (Atkinson, Eccles, Vroom) holds motivation = expectancy of success × value of goal; if either is near zero motivation is near zero, so a valued but seemingly unattainable goal yields low effort.

concept: Video recording as most objective micro-teaching feedback
must_teach: In micro-teaching, a video recording gives the most objective feedback because it can be replayed and is free from observer memory and bias; supervisor and peer comments are useful but filtered through perception.

concept: Fishbowl technique vs buzz group, panel, round robin
must_teach: Fishbowl: an inner circle discusses while an outer circle observes content and process and later comments, possibly swapping places. Buzz groups are brief simultaneous small-group discussions; panel is experts under a moderator; round robin gives each member a turn.

concept: OBE levels: course outcomes, programme outcomes, programme educational objectives
must_teach: In OBE, course outcomes state what students can do at the end of a course; programme outcomes and programme-specific outcomes state attainments at graduation; programme educational objectives describe what graduates achieve a few years into their careers.

concept: Achievement test scores lack a true zero
must_teach: A ratio scale needs an absolute zero meaning complete absence; tests sample only part of a subject, so a score of zero is not zero knowledge and 80 is not twice 40. Scores do show order.

concept: Basic requirements of a teacher: subject competence, communication
must_teach: Basic requirements of teaching include competence in content, communication skill, understanding of learners and methods. Fair evaluation requires transparency and accountability, not unchecked authority to grade.

concept: Same examination summative for students, formative for course
must_teach: An examination is summative for students when it decides their grades at the end; using its item-wise results to improve the course for the next batch is a formative use. Purpose and user decide the label.

concept: Honey and Mumford's four learning styles
must_teach: Honey and Mumford's styles, linked to Kolb's cycle: activists plunge into experience; reflectors stand back, gather data and observe before concluding; theorists integrate observations into logical theories; pragmatists try ideas out in practice.

concept: Moreno's sociodrama vs psychodrama
must_teach: J. L. Moreno distinguished psychodrama (an individual's private problems, therapeutic) from sociodrama (problems shared by a group or community). Classroom role play on social issues like dowry is sociodrama.

concept: Schedules of reinforcement and resistance to extinction
must_teach: Variable-ratio schedules produce responding most resistant to extinction because the end of reinforcement is not noticed. Continuous reinforcement gives fastest acquisition but fastest extinction; fixed-ratio and fixed-interval schedules are more predictable.

concept: Armstrong's heuristic method: learner as discoverer
must_teach: H. E. Armstrong's heuristic method places the learner in the position of a discoverer, finding things out by own observation and experiment; the teacher sets problems and guides but tells as little as possible.

concept: Overhead projector advantages vs slide projector and epidiascope
must_teach: The OHP projects transparencies brightly in a lit room with the teacher facing the class. Slide projectors need a darkened room; opaque objects need an episcope/epidiascope; OHP needs electricity and shows no motion or sound.

concept: Understanding level more thoughtful; associated with Morrison
must_teach: Understanding level teaching is more thoughtful than memory level because learners see relationships and use principles; the model is associated with Morrison, but the attribution does not explain thoughtfulness.

concept: Bourdieu's cultural capital as learner-related home factor
must_teach: Cultural capital (Bourdieu) is knowledge, language habits and familiarity with educated culture passed on by families and rewarded by institutions; first-generation students lack exposure, not ability. Bridge courses and mentoring help.

concept: Reliability necessary but not sufficient for validity
must_teach: Reliability is consistency; validity is measuring what the test claims. A test can be reliable but not valid (consistently measuring the wrong thing), but cannot be valid without being reliable.

concept: Limitations of reflective level: maturity prerequisite, time-consuming
must_teach: Reflective level teaching presupposes a knowledge base and capacity for abstract reasoning, so it does not suit young or unprepared learners; it is slow and takes more time than memory-level teaching.

concept: Standard error of measurement as band around obtained score
must_teach: The standard error of measurement estimates spread of obtained scores around a person's true score (e.g. 60 ± 3 gives 57-63); higher reliability gives smaller SEM. Standard deviation describes spread across a group.

concept: Parts of a rubric: criteria, scale levels, descriptors
must_teach: A rubric has criteria (aspects judged), a scale of performance levels, and descriptors (wording in each cell describing what that level of that criterion looks like), which make scoring consistent.

concept: LMS tracks and reports learner progress
must_teach: A learning management system (e.g. Moodle) adds enrolment, assignments with deadlines, auto-scored quizzes, grade books and progress tracking and reporting to file storage and sharing; tracking is its distinguishing feature.

concept: Piaget's centration in pre-operational stage
must_teach: Centration is the pre-operational child's focus on one striking feature (e.g. height of water) neglecting others, causing failure on conservation tasks. Conservation, reversibility and seriation appear in the concrete operational stage.

concept: Order of top levels in original vs revised Bloom
must_teach: In Bloom's 1956 taxonomy Evaluation is at the top above Synthesis; in the 2001 revision Create (former Synthesis) is placed above Evaluate. Evaluation means judging value using internal evidence or external criteria.

concept: Institutional climate affects teacher morale
must_teach: Institutional climate (leadership, recognition, participation in decisions, staff relations) shapes teacher morale. The institution also fixes the academic calendar, but that function does not explain morale.

concept: Creating a 'felt problem' at the reflective level
must_teach: Reflective level teaching begins with a felt problem: a genuine difficulty or perplexity, e.g. data that contradict learners' beliefs. Recall of earlier lessons, dictated definitions or announced conclusions create no such tension.

concept: Synectics model (William Gordon) uses analogies for creativity
must_teach: Synectics (William Gordon), a personal-family model, develops creativity by 'making the strange familiar and the familiar strange' using direct analogy, personal analogy and compressed conflict. Inquiry training (Suchman) trains investigation of puzzling events; concept attainment (Bruner) uses examples and non-examples; jurisprudential inquiry addresses public policy issues.

concept: Simpson's adaptation level vs mechanism and origination
must_teach: In Simpson's taxonomy, adaptation is modifying well-developed movement patterns to fit special requirements or new situations; mechanism is habitual performance; origination (highest) is creating entirely new movement patterns.

concept: Learner-centred methods aid retention through learner activity
must_teach: In learner-centred methods learners are active: what they work out, discuss and apply is processed more deeply and retained longer. Passive learners and an active teacher characterise teacher-centred methods.

concept: Slavin's STAD vs Jigsaw, Think-Pair-Share, Group Investigation
must_teach: STAD (Slavin): teaching, mixed-team study, individual quizzes, team recognition based on improvement points over each member's past average. Jigsaw divides content among members who teach one another; Think-Pair-Share is individual thought, pair discussion, sharing; Group Investigation (Thelen/Sharan) has groups inquire into subtopics.

concept: Nature of individual differences
must_teach: Individual differences exist in physical, mental, emotional and social traits, and are differences of degree (quantitative) and kind (qualitative). Uniform teaching does not eliminate them and often widens gaps.

concept: Models vs specimens as three-dimensional aids
must_teach: A model is an enlarged, reduced or simplified representation used when the real object is too large, small or inaccessible. A specimen is a real object or sample representing its class (rock, leaf, insect).

concept: Motivating learners as a function of teaching
must_teach: Learning needs the learner's own attention and effort; since nobody can learn on another's behalf, arousing and sustaining motivation is a necessary function of teaching.

concept: Skill of questioning: ask, pause, then name
must_teach: Putting the question to the whole class, pausing, then naming a student keeps every student thinking; naming first lets others relax. Components of questioning include clarity, relevance, pausing and distribution of questions.

concept: CBCS letter grade A = Very Good, 8 points
must_teach: UGC CBCS scale: O Outstanding 10, A+ Excellent 9, A Very Good 8, B+ Good 7, B Above Average 6, C Average 5, P Pass 4, F Fail 0.
flag: DATED: per UGC CBCS guidelines 2015 — verify still current

concept: Glaser's Basic Teaching Model components in sequence
must_teach: Robert Glaser's Basic Teaching Model: instructional objectives, entering behaviour, instructional procedures, performance assessment, linked by feedback loops.

concept: Maxims: known to unknown, simple to complex, particular to general, indefinite to definite
must_teach: Accepted maxims include known to unknown (consistent with Ausubel's prior knowledge), simple to complex (not complex to simple), particular to general (inductive), and indefinite to definite (refining vague ideas into clear ones).

concept: Learning and development: Vygotsky vs Piaget
must_teach: Vygotsky held that good learning, aimed at the ZPD, runs ahead of and leads development. Piaget held that the developmental stage reached largely sets the limits of what can be learnt.

concept: Krathwohl's affective taxonomy levels and date
must_teach: Krathwohl, Bloom and Masia (1964) affective levels: receiving (awareness, willingness to receive, selected attention), responding, valuing, organisation, characterisation (highest).

concept: Meaning of percentile rank
must_teach: A percentile rank gives the percentage of the reference group scoring below a given score (PR 80 = 80 per cent scored below). It differs from percentage of marks, which compares with the maximum possible.

concept: Adolescents' peer orientation suits group methods
must_teach: Late adolescents seek company and approval of peers and learn readily from one another, so group projects and discussions suit undergraduate learners.

concept: Number of SWAYAM PRABHA DTH channels
must_teach: SWAYAM PRABHA is a group of DTH channels telecasting educational programmes 24x7, free through DD Free Dish; it began in 2017 with 32 channels and was later expanded (stated as 48 per MoE/PIB March 2026).
flag: DATED: says SWAYAM PRABHA has 48 channels citing MoE PIB note on PM e-Vidya, March 2026 (launched 2017 with 32; later 40) — verify current figure and source

concept: Definitions of teaching: B. O. Smith, Morrison, Gage
must_teach: B. O. Smith: teaching is a system of actions intended to induce learning. Morrison: intimate contact between a more mature and a less mature personality. Gage: a form of interpersonal influence aimed at changing another's behaviour potential.

concept: Knowles's learning contract in self-directed learning
must_teach: A learning contract (recommended by Knowles) is a written agreement drawn up in advance by an adult learner with a facilitator stating objectives, resources, evidence of accomplishment and criteria. A portfolio collects evidence of work already done.

concept: Portfolio: purposeful selection and student reflection
must_teach: A portfolio is a purposeful collection of selected work against stated criteria, with the student's reflection on why each piece was chosen and what it shows; collecting everything without selection is merely a folder.

concept: Herbartian steps and their classroom activities
must_teach: Herbartian steps: preparation (recall related previous knowledge), presentation (introduce new material), comparison/association, generalisation (frame a rule from the facts), application (use the rule in new situations). Some lists add a statement of aim and recapitulation.

concept: Dale's cone bands and Bruner's modes of representation
must_teach: Dale's cone is read in three parts matching Bruner: bottom bands (direct, contrived, dramatised experiences) are doing/enactive; middle bands (demonstrations to still pictures) are observing/iconic; top bands (visual and verbal symbols) are symbolising/symbolic.

concept: Computing credits: lecture and practical hours
must_teach: Under UGC CBCS, one credit = one hour of lecture or tutorial, or two hours of practical work, per week over a semester; 3 lecture hours + 2 practical hours = 3 + 1 = 4 credits.

concept: Memory level teaching is teacher-centred
must_teach: At the memory level the teacher chooses content, fixes its order, presents and tests it; learners receive and reproduce. Learners do not select content or sequence.

concept: Task sense vs achievement sense of teaching (Ryle)
must_teach: Philosophers distinguish teaching in the task sense (trying; one may teach though nobody learns) from the achievement sense (succeeding; saying something was taught implies it was learnt, as selling implies buying).

concept: Variety of methods justified without fixed exclusive learning styles
must_teach: Teachers should vary methods and media because classes are diverse and content demands different modes. Learners have preferences, not exclusive channels; fixed learning styles are not supported by evidence.

concept: Stages of a seminar session
must_teach: A seminar session: chairperson introduces the theme and speaker, the paper is presented, participants discuss and question, and the chairperson sums up and closes.

concept: Puentedura's SAMR levels
must_teach: SAMR (Puentedura): Substitution (technology replaces a tool, no functional change), Augmentation (functional improvement, e.g. spell-check), Modification (task significantly redesigned), Redefinition (previously inconceivable tasks).

concept: Formative evaluation gives feedback to teacher and learner
must_teach: Formative evaluation, conducted while change is possible, gives feedback to the teacher on teaching effectiveness and to the learner on progress. Summative evaluation is used for certification, a separate fact.

concept: Distinguishing understanding-level from reflective-level outcomes
must_teach: Applying principles to familiar types of problems shows understanding level; judging unfamiliar, open problems by weighing evidence requires reflective level. Rote learners could not solve even the familiar problems.

concept: Functions of evaluation: instructional, administrative, guidance, research
must_teach: Evaluation functions: instructional (feedback to teaching and learning), administrative (promotion, selection, certification), guidance (educational and vocational choices), research (data for studies).

concept: Integrity and confidentiality in examination duties
must_teach: The code of professional ethics requires teachers to perform examination duties (setting, invigilation, evaluation) with honesty and confidentiality; leaking papers is a serious breach, with no exemption for relatives. Teacher autonomy does not cover disclosure.

concept: Classical conditioning of emotional responses
must_teach: A neutral stimulus (classroom) paired with an unconditioned stimulus (humiliation) becomes a conditioned stimulus evoking anxiety; involuntary emotional reactions are classically conditioned. Operant conditioning shapes voluntary behaviour by consequences.

concept: Knowles's later view: pedagogy-andragogy continuum
must_teach: Knowles first opposed andragogy to pedagogy but later treated them as ends of a continuum; adults who are complete novices may need teacher direction at first, moving to self-direction as competence grows.

concept: Handling unprepared students in a flipped classroom
must_teach: In a flipped course, re-lecturing for unprepared students removes the incentive to prepare; a brief entry quiz or task holds students accountable while the planned in-class activity proceeds.

concept: Good teaching judged by learning; flexible and democratic
must_teach: Good teaching is judged by the learning it produces, not syllabus coverage, and is flexible and democratic, adapting methods to learners rather than rigid and authoritarian.

concept: Intervening variables are selected and organised by the teacher
must_teach: Teacher = independent variable, learner = dependent variable, content/methods/strategies = intervening variables; the teacher selects and organises the intervening variables, through which the teacher's influence reaches the learner.

concept: Placement evaluation: prerequisites and prior mastery
must_teach: Placement evaluation checks whether learners have the prerequisites and whether they have already achieved the intended outcomes; those already proficient should skip ahead or receive enrichment/advanced work.

concept: Ranking objectives by revised taxonomy level
must_teach: Revised taxonomy order: Remember, Understand, Apply, Analyse, Evaluate, Create. Formulating a proposal = Create (highest); critiquing against criteria = Evaluate; distinguishing = Analyse; computing by known procedure = Apply.

concept: Bandura's reciprocal determinism
must_teach: Bandura's reciprocal determinism: personal factors (beliefs, expectations), behaviour and environment influence one another; this triadic interaction is central to social cognitive theory, rejecting one-way environmental or inner-drive determination.

concept: MOOCs: open enrolment but low completion rates
must_teach: MOOCs allow open, often free enrolment to huge numbers, but completion rates are typically low (single digits to low double digits), partly because many enrol out of curiosity.

concept: Criteria for selecting support material: suitability, accuracy
must_teach: Support material should suit learners' level (too hard or too childish fails to communicate) and should be accurate and up to date; these are separate selection criteria.

concept: Features of reflective level teaching
must_teach: Reflective level teaching is problem-centred, develops a scientific attitude and requires a democratic teacher; the learner is the most active participant, not passive.

concept: Characteristics of adolescent learners
must_teach: Adolescents are capable of abstract thinking (formal operations), seek independence from parents, are concerned about body image, and show emotional intensity and fluctuation (not stability).

concept: Computing a z-score
must_teach: z = (score - mean) / SD; e.g. (65 - 50) / 10 = 1.5, meaning 1.5 standard deviations above the mean. A z-score is a norm-referenced standard score.

concept: Flynn effect vs Matthew effect
must_teach: The Flynn effect (James Flynn) is the generational rise in average IQ scores, attributed to nutrition, schooling and environment, showing intelligence is not fixed by heredity alone. The Matthew effect is accumulation of early advantage; Pygmalion and halo effects concern expectations and rating bias.

concept: Bruner's modes; scaffolding coined by Wood, Bruner and Ross
must_teach: Bruner's enactive mode represents through action, iconic through images, symbolic through language/symbols. 'Scaffolding' was introduced by Wood, Bruner and Ross (1976) and later linked to Vygotsky's ZPD.

concept: Gronlund's general objectives with specific learning outcomes
must_teach: Gronlund recommended stating a general instructional objective (e.g. understands principles) clarified by a sample of specific learning outcomes in behavioural terms. The single-behaviour format with condition and criterion is Mager's.

concept: Maslow's deficiency vs growth needs
must_teach: Maslow's deficiency needs are physiological, safety, belongingness and esteem (they cease to motivate once met); self-actualisation is a growth (being) need that continues to motivate as it is satisfied.

concept: SWAYAM, SWAYAM PRABHA, One Nation One Subscription, Shodhgangotri
must_teach: SWAYAM: online courses with credit transfer. SWAYAM PRABHA: educational TV via DTH. One Nation One Subscription (operational from January 2025): nationwide access to scholarly e-journals, succeeding consortia like e-ShodhSindhu. Shodhgangotri: synopses of research in progress.
flag: DATED: ONOS operational from 2025 and replacing e-ShodhSindhu — verify current status

concept: Branching programmes individualise path as well as pace
must_teach: In linear programming all learners take the same path, only pace varies; in branching programming the learner's response routes him to remedial frames or ahead, so both path and pace are individualised.

concept: Tolman's cognitive map and purposive behaviourism
must_teach: Tolman argued rats learnt the maze layout as a cognitive map (sign learning, purposive behaviourism), not a fixed chain of habits, which is why they took a new route when the usual path was blocked.

concept: Flanders' rule of two-thirds
must_teach: Flanders' rule of two-thirds: about two-thirds of class time someone is talking; two-thirds of that talk is teacher talk; two-thirds of teacher talk is direct influence (lecturing, directing, criticising).

concept: Constructive alignment of outcomes and assessment in OBE
must_teach: In OBE, assessment is aligned with stated outcomes because its purpose is to determine whether intended outcomes have been attained; constructive alignment (Biggs) links outcomes, teaching activities and assessment.

concept: Open-book examination requires application and analysis questions
must_teach: In open-book examinations recall questions lose value, so questions must demand application, interpretation, analysis and judgement, with books serving as tools, not answer keys.

concept: Negative discrimination index signals faulty item
must_teach: Discrimination index = proportion correct in upper group minus that in lower group; a negative value means more low scorers answered correctly, signalling an ambiguous stem, wrong key or misleading option; such items are revised or dropped. Difficulty is shown by facility value.

concept: Kounin's withitness, overlapping, momentum, smoothness
must_teach: Kounin: withitness is communicating awareness of everything happening in the room; overlapping is attending to two matters at once; momentum and smoothness concern lesson flow.

concept: Computing required SGPA to reach a target CGPA
must_teach: CGPA = total credit points / total credits. Points so far 40 × 6.0 = 240; target 60 × 6.5 = 390; needed 150 over 20 credits = SGPA 7.5. CGPA is credit-weighted, not a simple average of SGPAs.

concept: Definitions of project: Stevenson, Kilpatrick, Ballard
must_teach: Stevenson: 'a problematic act carried to completion in its natural setting'. Kilpatrick: 'a whole-hearted purposeful activity proceeding in a social environment'. Ballard: 'a bit of real life imported into the school'. Kilpatrick, Dewey's follower, developed the project method.

concept: Bigge on understanding: relationships and tool use
must_teach: Bigge described understanding as seeing relationships between particulars and generalisations and seeing the 'tool use' of a fact, i.e. what it can be used for. Remembering exact wording is memory level.

concept: Effective demonstration: predict, observe, explain
must_teach: A demonstration secures learning when students are asked to predict, observe and explain each step, engaging thinking and exposing misconceptions; announcing conclusions first or performing silently leaves them passive, and all must be able to see.

concept: Computer-based testing logs response time; validity still needed
must_teach: Computer-based testing logs every action, so response times and answer changes can be analysed; the delivery mode does not improve item quality, so validity must still be established.

concept: Gronlund's formula: evaluation = description + value judgement
must_teach: Gronlund: evaluation = quantitative description (measurement) + qualitative description (non-measurement) + value judgements about desirability. Judgement of worth turns description into evaluation.

concept: Brainwriting as variant of brainstorming
must_teach: Brainwriting generates ideas silently in writing (e.g. on cards) before discussion, so quiet members contribute equally; it keeps deferred judgement, then ideas are pooled and discussed. Buzz sessions are oral small-group talk; fishbowl has inner/outer circles.

concept: Guidelines for writing MCQs
must_teach: MCQ stems should present a single clear problem; distractors should be plausible to the uninformed; the key's position should be random, not patterned; 'all of the above' type options give clues and are best avoided.

concept: Psychological safety in the learning environment
must_teach: Treating errors as learning steps rather than ridiculing them builds psychological safety, so students participate and attempt hard tasks. It differs from laissez-faire (withdrawal of guidance) and from authoritarian or competitive climates.

concept: Conditioning lies lowest on the teaching continuum
must_teach: On the teaching continuum, activities are ranked by the role of the learner's understanding: conditioning, which relies on stimulus-response association and by-passes understanding, is at the bottom; training and instruction are higher; teaching is highest.

concept: Revised taxonomy categories and their 19 specific processes
must_teach: Apply: executing, implementing. Analyse: differentiating, organising, attributing. Evaluate: checking, critiquing. Create: generating, planning, producing. (Remember: recognising, recalling; Understand: interpreting, exemplifying, classifying, summarising, inferring, comparing, explaining.)

concept: Cross's barriers to adult learning
must_teach: K. Patricia Cross: situational barriers (circumstances such as job, family, cost, transport), institutional barriers (provider schedules, rules, fees), dispositional barriers (attitudes and self-perceptions such as feeling too old).

concept: Operations of the post-active phase of teaching
must_teach: Post-active operations: defining the exact dimensions of behaviour changes achieved, selecting testing devices and techniques, and changing strategies in light of evidence. Sizing up the class (perception of size and mood) is an interactive-phase operation.

concept: Team teaching: uses specialisation, joint planning, needs coordination
must_teach: Team teaching uses each teacher's special competence and requires joint planning, teaching and evaluation; it demands more coordination than individual teaching, which is its main practical difficulty.

concept: Content and methods as intervening variables
must_teach: Teacher = independent variable; learner = dependent variable; content, strategies and methods stand between and carry the teacher's influence, so they are intervening variables.

concept: Evidence for content validity, predictive validity, test-retest and inter-rater reliability
must_teach: Content validity: items correspond to syllabus/blueprint. Predictive validity: scores correlate with a later criterion. Test-retest reliability: correlation of the same test given twice. Inter-rater reliability: agreement between independent scorers.

concept: Dewey's five steps of reflective thinking
must_teach: Dewey's steps (How We Think): felt difficulty; its location and definition; suggestion of possible solutions; reasoning out implications of each; testing by observation or experiment leading to acceptance or rejection. The problem-solving method follows this order.

concept: Comparing levels of teaching: prerequisites, problem-centredness, teacher role, tests
must_teach: Each level builds on the one below (understanding presupposes facts); reflective level is problem-centred with the teacher as democratic guide and the learner active; teacher dominance marks memory level; essay-type tests suit reflective outcomes.

concept: Projected vs non-projected aids
must_teach: Non-projected aids are seen directly: chalkboard, charts, models, flash cards, flannel board. Filmstrips and overhead transparencies need a projector; the epidiascope is itself a projector for opaque objects and slides.

concept: Underachiever vs slow learner
must_teach: An underachiever has adequate or high measured ability but attains far below it, usually for motivational, emotional or environmental reasons. A slow learner has below-average ability and attains accordingly; dyscalculia is a specific learning disability in mathematics.

concept: Lecture: economical for large classes but largely one-way
must_teach: The lecture is economical, letting one teacher present an organised overview to many students quickly, useful for introducing topics; its weakness is one-way communication and comparatively passive learners.

concept: Ipsative (self-referenced) assessment
must_teach: Ipsative assessment judges a learner against his or her own earlier performance, reporting personal progress. Norm-referenced compares with other learners; criterion-referenced compares with a fixed external standard.

concept: Ausubel: reception-discovery and rote-meaningful are separate dimensions
must_teach: Ausubel treated reception vs discovery and rote vs meaningful as independent dimensions: reception (expository) learning can be meaningful and discovery can be rote. Learning is meaningful when new material is substantively related to existing cognitive structure.

concept: Flanders' categories: indirect vs direct teacher talk
must_teach: FIAC has ten categories: indirect teacher talk (1 accepts feelings, 2 praises/encourages, 3 accepts or uses students' ideas, 4 asks questions); direct teacher talk (5 lecturing, 6 giving directions, 7 criticising/justifying authority); student talk (8 response, 9 initiation); 10 silence or confusion.

concept: Presage, context, process, product variables in teaching research
must_teach: In Mitzel's and Dunkin and Biddle's model, presage variables are what teachers bring (formative experiences, training, traits); context variables concern pupils, school and community; process variables are observable classroom behaviours; product variables are pupil outcomes.

concept: Heutagogy as self-determined learning
must_teach: Heutagogy (Hase and Kenyon) is self-determined learning in which the learner decides what and how to learn and revises goals; it goes beyond andragogy (self-directed within a teacher-designed course). Peeragogy is peer-produced learning.

concept: Interpreting facility value and near-zero discrimination
must_teach: Facility value = proportion answering correctly (30/100 = 0.30). If upper and lower groups do equally well, discrimination index is near zero; such an item fails to separate able from weak and needs revision.

concept: Classifying behaviours into Krathwohl's affective levels
must_teach: Receiving = attending; Responding = active participation (e.g. volunteering comment); Valuing = attaching worth and commitment; Organisation = building a value system; Characterisation = a value system consistently governing behaviour.

concept: Methods and originators: Dalton Plan, heuristic, linear PI, brainstorming
must_teach: Helen Parkhurst: Dalton Plan (individual assignments/contracts). H. E. Armstrong: heuristic method. B. F. Skinner: linear programmed instruction. Alex Osborn: brainstorming.

concept: Levels of teaching are hierarchical; reflective level associated with Hunt
must_teach: Reflective teaching needs facts and understood relationships, so memory and understanding levels are its prerequisites. The reflective level is associated with Hunt (and Bigge), a separate fact not explaining the prerequisite.
flag: DOUBT: attributes reflective level to Hunt; attribution varies across texts (Hunt, Bigge, Hunt and Bigge) — guide should present consistently

concept: Mager's condition component of an objective
must_teach: Mager's three parts: performance (what the learner will do), condition (circumstances, e.g. 'given an outline map'), criterion (standard, e.g. '90 per cent accuracy').

concept: Teaching is intentional; learning may be incidental
must_teach: Teaching always involves intention to bring about learning, but learning is wider and may occur incidentally from unplanned experience and observation, so learning can occur without teaching.

concept: Analytic vs holistic rubric vs checklist
must_teach: An analytic rubric scores separate criteria and describes levels for each, giving a profile and a total; a holistic rubric gives one overall score; a checklist records only presence or absence; an anecdotal record is a narrative of observed incidents.

concept: Cattell's fluid vs crystallised intelligence across age
must_teach: Cattell: fluid intelligence is reasoning in novel situations and tends to decline from early adulthood; crystallised intelligence is accumulated knowledge and skills (vocabulary, information) and is maintained or grows with age.

concept: Identifying highest level of teaching reached in a lesson
must_teach: Recall alone is memory level; explaining relationships and applying to familiar examples is understanding level; reflective level requires an open problematic situation investigated critically without a ready procedure.

concept: Order of Dale's cone bands from concrete to abstract
must_teach: Dale's cone base upward: direct purposeful experiences, contrived experiences, dramatised experiences, demonstrations, study trips, exhibits, television, motion pictures, recordings/radio/still pictures, visual symbols, verbal symbols (apex).

concept: Herbartian steps vs Morrison's steps; presentation common
must_teach: Herbartian steps: preparation, presentation, comparison/association, generalisation, application. Morrison's steps: exploration, presentation, assimilation, organisation, recitation. Only presentation appears in both.

concept: SWAYAM credit-transfer ceiling under UGC 2021 Regulations
must_teach: UGC (Credit Framework for Online Learning Courses through SWAYAM) Regulations 2021 allow up to 40 per cent of total courses offered in a programme in a semester through SWAYAM; the 2016 Regulations had a 20 per cent ceiling.
flag: DATED: credit-transfer limit (40% under 2021 Regulations, 20% under 2016) — verify no later amendment (e.g. NEP/ABC-related changes)

concept: Criterion-referenced tests certify mastery; norm-referenced spread scores
must_teach: Certifying mastery of minimum competencies needs comparison with a fixed standard (criterion-referenced). Norm-referenced tests are built to spread scores for ranking; rank does not show mastery.

concept: Components of the skill of stimulus variation
must_teach: Stimulus variation components: teacher movement, gestures, change in speech pattern, pausing, focusing, change in interaction style, oral-visual switching. Set induction secures attention only at lesson opening by linking to previous knowledge.

concept: Piaget's assimilation vs accommodation
must_teach: Assimilation fits a new experience into an existing schema (calling a cow a 'big dog'); accommodation changes a schema or creates a new one when experience does not fit (forming the category 'cow').

concept: SWAYAM PRABHA reaches learners via DTH without internet
must_teach: SWAYAM PRABHA telecasts curriculum-based programmes 24x7 on DTH channels for learners without internet; SWAYAM, e-PG Pathshala and Virtual Labs are web-based and need internet.

concept: Negative reinforcement: removing an aversive to increase behaviour
must_teach: Reinforcement increases behaviour, punishment decreases it; positive adds, negative removes. Removing an unpleasant event (a tedious test) when the behaviour occurs, so the behaviour rises, is negative reinforcement.

concept: Operations in Jackson's pre-active, interactive, post-active phases
must_teach: Pre-active: fixing objectives, deciding content and strategies. Interactive: sizing up the class, diagnosing learners, action and reaction. Post-active: evaluating outcomes, selecting tests, revising strategies, reflecting.

concept: Adolescence: formal operations, Erikson's identity crisis, peer influence
must_teach: Piaget: hypothetico-deductive reasoning appears in formal operations. Erikson: adolescence is identity vs role confusion; intimacy vs isolation belongs to young adulthood. Peer influence increases in adolescence.

concept: Crowder's branching (intrinsic) programming
must_teach: In Crowder's branching (intrinsic) programming each frame ends with a multiple-choice question and wrong choices lead to remedial frames before returning to the main sequence. Skinner's linear programming takes all learners through the same small steps with minimal errors.

concept: Yerkes-Dodson law: inverted-U relation of arousal and performance
must_teach: The Yerkes-Dodson law describes an inverted U: performance improves with arousal (anxiety) up to an optimum and then declines, and the optimum is lower for difficult tasks. Moderate anxiety can facilitate performance; it does not rise steadily.

concept: Measurement vs evaluation: scope and value judgement
must_teach: Measurement assigns numbers according to rules and is quantitative; evaluation is wider, using quantitative measurement and qualitative description and adding a value judgement against objectives.

concept: 2001 revision: Synthesis renamed Create and placed above Evaluate
must_teach: In the 2001 revision, Evaluation became Evaluate at level five and Synthesis, renamed Create, moved to the top; categories became verbs and Knowledge became Remember.

concept: Hawthorne effect vs Pygmalion, John Henry, halo
must_teach: The Hawthorne effect is improved performance due to awareness of being studied or given attention. Pygmalion works through teacher expectations; John Henry effect is the control group working harder to compete; halo effect is a rating bias spreading from one trait.

concept: Order of Dave's psychomotor taxonomy
must_teach: Dave's psychomotor levels: imitation, manipulation, precision, articulation, naturalisation.

concept: Training vs instruction, teaching, conditioning
must_teach: Training builds a specific skill through repeated practice to a set standard without concern for understanding; instruction imparts structured knowledge; teaching aims at understanding and judgement; conditioning establishes stimulus-response connections.

concept: Symposium: prepared papers on aspects, no inter-speaker conversation
must_teach: In a symposium several speakers present prepared statements on different aspects of one theme in turn, without conversing, followed by audience questions; in a panel discussion members converse informally under a moderator.

concept: No single factor suffices; method effect depends on learner readiness
must_teach: Subject mastery is necessary but not sufficient for effective teaching: communication skill, method, support material and learner characteristics also matter. The effect of a method depends partly on learners' readiness and prior knowledge.

concept: Synchronous, asynchronous, blended learning; xMOOC vs cMOOC
must_teach: Recorded lectures at one's own time are asynchronous; live webinars are synchronous; blended learning combines face-to-face and online. cMOOCs are connectivist and learner-networked; xMOOCs are structured, instructor-led video-and-quiz courses.

concept: Knowles: self-concept moves from dependence to self-direction
must_teach: Knowles's first andragogical assumption: with maturity self-concept moves from dependence towards self-direction; adults therefore resist being treated as dependent recipients of instruction.

concept: Computing SGPA as credit-weighted mean
must_teach: SGPA = Σ(credits × grade points) / Σ credits; e.g. (54 + 14 + 16) / 10 = 8.4. A simple average of grade points ignores credits and is wrong.

concept: Diagnostic beyond formative; placement concerns entry performance
must_teach: Formative evaluation monitors progress; diagnostic evaluation probes causes of persistent difficulties. Placement evaluation concerns entry performance before instruction, a different type.

concept: Learning theorists: Bandura, Köhler, Thorndike, Tolman
must_teach: Bandura: observational learning. Köhler: insight learning (chimpanzee studies). Thorndike: law of effect. Tolman: latent learning (learning without reinforcement, shown later).

concept: Inductive vs deductive methods: direction, discovery, time
must_teach: Induction moves from particular examples to a rule and from concrete to abstract; it suits discovery but takes time. Deduction states the rule first and applies it, moving from abstract to concrete, and covers content faster.

concept: Micro-teaching cycle sequence
must_teach: Micro-teaching cycle: plan, teach, feedback, re-plan, re-teach, re-feedback; re-teaching is usually to a different group of pupils.

concept: Theories of intelligence: Spearman, Thurstone, Guilford, Sternberg
must_teach: Spearman: two-factor theory (g and s). Thurstone: seven primary mental abilities. Guilford: structure-of-intellect (operations, contents, products). Sternberg: triarchic theory (analytical, creative, practical).

concept: Computerised adaptive testing vs linear fixed-form and LOFT
must_teach: In CAT the program estimates ability after each response and selects the next item to match, so candidates see different items and fewer are needed. Linear fixed-form gives all the same items; linear-on-the-fly assembles a unique form before the test without adapting.

concept: Metacognitive knowledge in the revised taxonomy
must_teach: The knowledge dimension has factual, conceptual, procedural and metacognitive knowledge; metacognitive knowledge (added in the revision) is knowledge of cognition in general and of one's own cognition, including strategies and self-knowledge.

concept: Models of teaching and their originators (Bruner, Suchman, Ausubel, Oliver and Shaver)
must_teach: Concept attainment model is based on Bruner; inquiry training on Suchman; advance organiser on Ausubel; jurisprudential inquiry on Oliver and Shaver.

concept: Basic requirements of teaching: content knowledge plus pedagogy plus knowledge of learners
must_teach: Subject knowledge alone is insufficient; it must be joined to pedagogical skill. Knowing learners' previous knowledge, abilities and interests is equally a requirement of teaching.

concept: Synchronous vs asynchronous online learning
must_teach: Synchronous learning happens at the same time in real time (e.g. live webinar); freedom from a common time defines asynchronous learning.

concept: Bloom's Knowledge category includes knowledge of criteria; level set by verb
must_teach: Bloom's 1956 Knowledge category covers knowledge of specifics, of ways and means (including knowledge of criteria) and of universals. Recalling criteria is Knowledge; using criteria to judge would be Evaluation.

concept: Workshop: participants do practical work and produce a product
must_teach: A workshop is defined by participants' practical work yielding a product, with short expert input. Seminars and symposia centre on presenting and discussing papers; a conference is a larger meeting for exchange.

concept: Morrison's five steps vs Herbartian five steps
must_teach: Morrison: exploration, presentation, assimilation, organisation, recitation. Herbart (formal steps): preparation, presentation, comparison/association, generalisation, application. Only presentation is common; organisation is Morrison's alone.

concept: Stimulus generalisation in classical conditioning
must_teach: Stimulus generalisation: a response conditioned to one stimulus is evoked by similar stimuli. Discrimination is responding only to the original stimulus; response generalisation is one stimulus evoking several similar responses; spontaneous recovery is return of an extinguished response.

concept: Test-retest reliability gives coefficient of stability
must_teach: Test-retest gives coefficient of stability; parallel forms give equivalence; split-half and Kuder-Richardson give internal consistency; parallel forms after an interval give stability and equivalence.

concept: Classifying influences into institution, facilities, environment factors
must_teach: Administrative support and leadership are institution factors; equipment like projectors, labs, libraries are instructional facilities; physical conditions like noise and light and psychological climate are learning environment.

concept: An assessment's function depends on use; can be formative and summative
must_teach: Feedback that guides further learning is a formative use; counting marks toward the final grade is a summative use; one assessment can serve both functions.

concept: Case method presents realistic problem; role play is unscripted
must_teach: A case describes a real or realistic situation for analysis and decision. Role play gives players a situation and role to improvise; a memorised script makes it dramatisation.

concept: Marcia's identity statuses: exploration and commitment
must_teach: Moratorium = exploration without commitment; diffusion = neither; foreclosure = commitment without exploration; achievement = commitment after exploration.

concept: Concrete-to-abstract vs particular-to-general maxims are distinct
must_teach: Concrete to abstract concerns kind of experience (things to ideas); particular to general concerns scope (cases to rule) and is the basis of the inductive method. They are separate maxims.

concept: Projection devices and the material each projects
must_teach: Episcope projects opaque pictures/objects by reflected light; slide projector (diascope) projects small mounted transparent slides; OHP projects large writable transparencies; LCD projector shows computer output.

concept: Motivation theories: Alderfer ERG, Herzberg, Vroom, McClelland
must_teach: Alderfer: existence, relatedness, growth (ERG). Herzberg: hygiene factors and motivators. Vroom: valence, instrumentality, expectancy. McClelland: needs for achievement, affiliation, power.

concept: Self-assessment and peer assessment can be formative without marks
must_teach: Self-assessment is mainly reflection against criteria and need not produce a grade. Peer assessment can be confined to comments to improve drafts, without marks.

concept: Cognitive processes under each category of revised Bloom's taxonomy
must_teach: Remember: recognising, recalling. Understand: interpreting, exemplifying, classifying, summarising, inferring, comparing, explaining. Apply: executing, implementing. Analyse: differentiating, organising, attributing. Metacognitive knowledge includes self-knowledge.

concept: Aptitude-treatment interaction (Cronbach and Snow)
must_teach: Cronbach and Snow's aptitude-treatment interaction: a method's effect depends on its interaction with learner characteristics, so the same method gives different results with different learners; no method is best for all.

concept: Reflective level: learners reach and test generalisations themselves
must_teach: At understanding level the teacher explains generalisations and learners grasp and apply them; at reflective level learners face a problem and arrive at and test generalisations through their own inquiry.

concept: Components of the skill of probing questioning
must_teach: Probing components: prompting (hints after no/wrong answer), seeking further information, refocusing (relating answer to another situation), redirection (same question to other students), increasing critical awareness (asking for justification).

concept: Sequence of steps in educational diagnosis and remediation
must_teach: Diagnosis order: identify students with difficulty, locate specific areas of difficulty, find causes, then plan remedial instruction.

concept: Seligman's learned helplessness
must_teach: Learned helplessness (Seligman): after uncontrollable failure, learners believe outcomes do not depend on their actions and stop trying even when success is possible. Test anxiety is fear interfering during tests; field dependence is a cognitive style; identity diffusion is Marcia's status.

concept: Guilford's divergent vs convergent production
must_teach: Guilford: convergent production seeks one correct answer; divergent production generates many answers and underlies creativity. Unusual-uses tests measure divergent production, scored for fluency, flexibility, originality.

concept: Computing CGPA as credit-weighted average of SGPAs
must_teach: CGPA = sum of (semester credits x SGPA) / total credits; not the simple average of SGPAs. Example: (160+140+60)/50 = 7.2.

concept: Memory level is necessary but insufficient; does not develop critical thought
must_teach: Memory level teaching supplies facts needed for higher levels but does not develop independent critical thinking; that is the outcome of reflective level teaching.

concept: Post-active (reflection) and pre-active (planning) phases
must_teach: Analysing a lesson already taught is post-active (evaluation, reflection); planning the next lesson is pre-active; interactive is classroom delivery. Phases feed into each other cyclically.

concept: National Academic Depository stores degrees and mark-sheets digitally
must_teach: National Academic Depository (accessed through DigiLocker) is an online store of academic awards for verification; Academic Bank of Credits records credits earned; NDLI is a digital library; Shodhganga holds theses.
flag: NEW?: NAD and ABC fit across 4.6 and 6.7; ensure guide names NAD (currently not in outline). Verify current NAD-DigiLocker arrangement.

concept: Constructivism treats errors as information about learners' ideas
must_teach: Constructivism: learners build knowledge by testing existing ideas against experience; errors reveal those ideas and are opportunities for restructuring understanding.

concept: Krathwohl's Responding level and its sub-levels (acquiescence)
must_teach: Affective taxonomy: Receiving, Responding, Valuing, Organisation, Characterisation. Responding sub-levels: acquiescence in responding, willingness to respond, satisfaction in response; compliant action is Responding, mere attention is Receiving.

concept: Morrison's recitation step means oral presentation of mastered unit
must_teach: Recitation is Morrison's fifth and last step; it means the pupil orally presents the mastered unit in own words, not rote reproduction.

concept: Knowles' andragogy assumption: orientation to learning (problem-centred)
must_teach: Knowles' assumptions: self-concept, role of experience, readiness to learn (when social-role tasks demand), orientation to learning (immediate application, problem-centred), motivation (internal), need to know.

concept: Availability of facilities does not ensure use; library as instructional facility
must_teach: Libraries are instructional facilities, but they go unused when teaching does not require independent reading, hours are inconvenient, or students lack library skills; classification does not explain use.

concept: Percentile rank is norm-referenced; percentage of objectives mastered is criterion-referenced
must_teach: Norm-referenced scores locate a student among others (percentile rank); criterion-referenced scores describe mastery of a defined domain (percentage of objectives mastered) without comparison.

concept: Strengths and limits of lecture and demonstration methods
must_teach: Demonstration is more concrete than lecture, but the teacher performs while learners watch, so it gives no hands-on practice. Lecture efficiently transmits information but is not suited to developing skills.

concept: Types of validity: content, concurrent, predictive, construct
must_teach: Content validity: adequate sampling of the course. Concurrent: agreement with a criterion available now. Predictive: forecasting later performance. Construct: reflects the theoretical trait.

concept: Crowder's branching vs Skinner's linear programmed instruction
must_teach: Crowder's branching: larger frames, multiple-choice responses, wrong choices lead to remedial frames (errors used diagnostically). Skinner's linear: small steps, constructed responses, near-errorless learning.

concept: Indian model of micro-teaching vs Stanford model
must_teach: Stanford model used real pupils and videotape feedback. Indian model (Passi/NCERT) uses peers as pupils under simulated conditions and feedback from supervisors and peer observers, without costly equipment; full cycle and one-skill principle retained.

concept: Teaching as a triadic relation
must_teach: Teaching is logically triadic: someone (teacher) teaches something (content) to someone (learner). That teaching is a profession is a separate social fact and does not explain the triadic structure.

concept: Analytic method works from unknown conclusion back to known data
must_teach: Analytic method proceeds from the unknown (conclusion) back to the known (data), showing why each step is taken; synthetic presents proof from data to conclusion; deduction applies a general rule to cases; induction goes from cases to rule.
flag: NEW?: analytic-synthetic method not explicitly in 4.4 list; add to 4.4 or 1.6 (maxim analysis to synthesis).

concept: Test, measurement and evaluation distinguished
must_teach: A test is an instrument; measurement is the process of assigning numbers to performance; evaluation interprets numbers with other evidence and judges worth against objectives.

concept: First levels of Dave, Simpson, Harrow and Krathwohl taxonomies
must_teach: Dave begins with Imitation; Simpson with Perception; Harrow with Reflex movements; Krathwohl (affective) with Receiving.

concept: Relative grading is norm-referenced; absolute grading is criterion-referenced
must_teach: Relative grading awards grades by position in the group (norm-referenced); absolute grading uses fixed pre-set standards (criterion-referenced).

concept: Diorama vs mock-up vs cut-away model
must_teach: Diorama: three-dimensional miniature scene with figures before a painted background. Mock-up: simplified working replica for training. Cut-away model: shows the inside of an object. Specimen: real object or sample.

concept: Integration vs inclusion of learners with disabilities
must_teach: Integration places the learner in the regular setting without changing the system; inclusion requires the institution to change, removing barriers and providing accommodation. Segregation means separate settings; exclusion means denial of education.

concept: Number of SWAYAM National Coordinators (ten per MoE 2026)
must_teach: SWAYAM National Coordinators listed as ten: NPTEL, UGC, AICTE, CEC, IGNOU, IIM Bangalore, NITTTR, INI, NCERT, NIOS; older sources list nine.
flag: DATED: says ten National Coordinators citing MoE March 2026 note on PM e-Vidya (older sources list nine; INI addition) — verify current list and count.

concept: Order of Gagné's nine events of instruction
must_teach: Gagné's events: gaining attention, informing learners of objective, stimulating recall, presenting stimulus, providing guidance, eliciting performance, providing feedback, assessing performance, enhancing retention and transfer.

concept: SWAYAM PRABHA is free DTH broadcast; SWAYAM gives credits
must_teach: SWAYAM PRABHA is one-way DTH television, free on DD Free Dish, needing no internet and offering no assessment. SWAYAM is the interactive MOOC platform with quizzes, exams and credit transfer.

concept: Vygotsky's actual vs potential development levels and ZPD
must_teach: Actual development = independent problem-solving; potential development = problem-solving with guidance from a more capable person; ZPD is the distance between the two.

concept: UGC ten-point grade scale: F and Ab carry zero
must_teach: UGC CBCS ten-point scale: O 10, A+ 9, A 8, B+ 7, B 6, C 5, P 4, F 0, Ab 0. Credits of F/Ab courses count in SGPA denominator.
flag: DOUBT: claim that F/Ab credits still count in SGPA calculation follows the UGC illustration but practice varies by university — verify wording.

concept: Conservation is achieved in concrete operational stage via reversibility
must_teach: Pre-operational children fail conservation tasks; conservation is the chief achievement of the concrete operational stage and depends on understanding reversibility.

concept: Order and meaning of Dave's psychomotor levels
must_teach: Dave's order: imitation, manipulation, precision, articulation, naturalisation. Articulation = coordinating a series of actions harmoniously; copying a model is imitation.

concept: Flipped classroom is one model of blended learning
must_teach: Blended learning combines face-to-face and online learning; the flipped classroom (content online first, class time for application) is one blended model; rotation and flex models are blended but not flipped.

concept: Checklist vs rating scale vs rubric
must_teach: Checklist records presence/absence; rating scale records degree on a numerical or verbal scale; a rubric adds descriptors of performance at each level (analytic per criterion, holistic overall).

concept: Validity ceiling equals square root of reliability (index of reliability)
must_teach: Maximum validity coefficient = square root of reliability coefficient (index of reliability); e.g. reliability 0.64 gives maximum validity 0.80.

concept: Support material vs instructional facilities
must_teach: Support material: aids and resources for particular content (charts, models, handouts, worksheets, slides). Instructional facilities: institutional infrastructure (halls, labs, libraries, networks).

concept: Direct vs indirect assessment tools in outcome-based education
must_teach: Direct assessment examines actual performance (tests, assignments, projects); indirect assessment gathers opinions about learning via surveys (course-exit, alumni, employer). Outcome attainment relies mainly on direct tools.
flag: NEW?: outcome-based education (CO/PO attainment, direct/indirect tools) not in outline; consider adding to 6.3 or 6.9.

concept: Order of bands in Dale's Cone of Experience
must_teach: Dale's cone from base: direct purposeful experiences, contrived experiences, dramatised experiences, demonstrations, study trips, exhibits, television, motion pictures, recordings/radio/still pictures, visual symbols, verbal symbols.

concept: Kohlberg's conventional level: law and order orientation
must_teach: Kohlberg: pre-conventional (punishment, self-interest), conventional (good boy/girl, law and order stage 4), post-conventional (social contract, universal principles that may override rules). Heteronomous is Piaget's term.

concept: Cooperative climate favours learning; competition not always harmful
must_teach: Research favours cooperative over competitive classroom structures for achievement and relationships, but moderate friendly competition (between groups or against one's own record) can motivate.

concept: Reflective level needs a democratic, open classroom
must_teach: Reflective level teaching requires freedom to doubt, question and propose alternatives, so it needs a democratic open climate; an authoritarian classroom denies this.

concept: Limits of academic freedom
must_teach: Academic freedom protects inquiry, expression of evidence-based (even controversial) views, criticism of theories and choice of method, but does not permit disregarding the prescribed curriculum or evaluation norms.

concept: Cumulative record vs portfolio, anecdotal record, sociogram
must_teach: Cumulative record: institution's year-by-year comprehensive record of a student. Portfolio: student's selection of work with reflection. Anecdotal record: single incidents. Sociogram: choices within a group.

concept: Evaluation methods at memory, understanding and reflective levels
must_teach: Memory level: oral and written recall tests. Understanding level: both objective-type and essay-type items. Reflective level: mainly essay-type tests.

concept: Teacher-centred vs learner-centred: roles and choice of approach
must_teach: Learner-centred teaching changes the teacher's role to designer and guide but does not make it unimportant, and uses formative assessment extensively. Teacher-centred exposition suits introducing unfamiliar content; choice depends on objectives, learners and content.

concept: Features of the Herbartian approach
must_teach: Herbartian approach: orderly presentation via formal steps, rests on doctrine of apperception, uses recitation and drill, and is teacher-centred.

concept: Correction for guessing formula S = R - W/(n-1)
must_teach: Correction for guessing: S = R - W/(n-1), n = number of options; omitted items are not counted. E.g. 40 - 12/3 = 36.

concept: Thorndike's law of readiness
must_teach: Law of readiness: when ready, acting satisfies and not acting annoys; when not ready, forced action annoys. Law of effect: consequences after a response; law of exercise: use and disuse.

concept: Kelley's upper and lower 27 per cent groups in item analysis
must_teach: Item analysis uses upper and lower 27 per cent of examinees ranked by total score (Kelley); for 200 examinees each group has 54.

concept: Raw scores need a norm or criterion frame of reference
must_teach: A raw score has little meaning alone; it must be interpreted against a norm (others' performance) or criterion (standard) to become information.

concept: Bandura's four sources of self-efficacy; mastery strongest
must_teach: Bandura's sources of self-efficacy: mastery experiences (strongest), vicarious experiences, verbal persuasion, physiological/emotional states.

concept: Psychological bases of maxims of teaching
must_teach: Known to unknown rests on Herbart's apperception; whole to part on Gestalt perception; simple to complex on graded difficulty; particular to general on inductive reasoning.

concept: Types of tutorial: supervision, group, practical
must_teach: Supervision tutorial: tutor with one or two students on their written work (Oxbridge). Group tutorial: small group clearing common difficulties after lectures. Practical tutorial: skills in lab or workshop.

concept: Bruner's theory of instruction features; discovery for all ages
must_teach: Bruner's theory of instruction (Toward a Theory of Instruction) addresses predisposition to learn, structure of knowledge, sequence and reinforcement. He held any subject can be taught in some honest form to any child, so discovery is not excluded for young children.

concept: Justifying with reasons is Evaluate (cognitive), not Valuing
must_teach: Justifying a choice against criteria is the cognitive process Evaluate; Valuing is affective, concerning attitude and commitment.

concept: Krathwohl's Receiving sub-levels: selected attention
must_teach: Receiving sub-levels: awareness, willingness to receive, controlled or selected attention. Responding begins only when the learner reacts.

concept: Flanders' categories: 8-9 student talk, 10 silence, questions indirect
must_teach: FIACS: categories 1-4 indirect teacher influence (4 = asking questions), 5-7 direct influence, 8-9 student talk, 10 silence/confusion. Only verbal behaviour is coded.

concept: Good teaching aims at learner independence, not dependence
must_teach: Good teaching gives guidance suited to learners' needs so that it can be withdrawn; its aim is an independent learner, not permanent dependence on the teacher.

concept: Knowles' readiness and experience are separate assumptions
must_teach: Knowles: readiness to learn arises from developmental tasks of social roles; adults have a large reservoir of experience as a resource. These are separate assumptions, neither causing the other.

concept: Incident method (Pigors) as variant of case method
must_teach: In the incident method (Paul Pigors) learners get a brief incident and must obtain remaining facts by questioning before analysis; in an ordinary case study full facts are given. In-basket method simulates handling a manager's papers.

concept: Evaluation is integral to teaching; communication a separate feature
must_teach: Evaluation is integral to teaching because the teacher must know whether objectives are achieved to adjust instruction. Teaching being communication is a separate characteristic.

concept: Problem-solving method vs project method
must_teach: Both involve purposeful learner activity, but problem-solving is chiefly mental and ends in a solution, while a project is carried out in a real-life setting and ends in a tangible product.

concept: Specific learning disabilities: dysgraphia, dyslexia, dyscalculia, dyspraxia
must_teach: Dysgraphia = writing difficulty (letter formation, spacing); dyslexia = reading; dyscalculia = number; dyspraxia = planning and coordination of movement.

concept: cMOOCs rest on connectivism (Siemens, Downes)
must_teach: cMOOCs, designed by Siemens and Downes on connectivist lines, have learners find, create and share content; connectivism sees learning as forming connections across networks. xMOOCs are content-delivery courses.

concept: Johnson and Johnson's social interdependence types
must_teach: Negative interdependence (competition): one succeeds only if others fail. Positive interdependence (cooperation): each succeeds only if others succeed. No interdependence (individualistic): results independent.

concept: Facility access is necessary but not sufficient for educational use
must_teach: Providing ICT facilities does not by itself change teaching methods; use depends on teacher skill, willingness, time and institutional support. Access is necessary but not sufficient.

concept: Teaching variables and independent/dependent variables in experiments
must_teach: In analysis of teaching, teacher is independent variable, learner dependent, and content/methods intervening. In an experiment, the manipulated factor (method) is independent and the measured outcome (achievement) is dependent.

concept: Adult experience as resource and possible hindrance
must_teach: Knowles saw experience as adults' richest resource, but it can also produce fixed habits, biases and assumptions that resist new learning, requiring unlearning.

concept: ePathshala (NCERT/CIET) vs e-PG Pathshala (UGC)
must_teach: ePathshala (NCERT's CIET) provides school textbooks and e-resources; e-PG Pathshala is UGC/INFLIBNET e-content for postgraduate courses; Shodhganga holds theses; NPTEL is IIT/IISc engineering content.

concept: Origin of formative/summative: Scriven (curriculum), Bloom (student learning)
must_teach: Scriven (1967) coined formative and summative evaluation for curriculum/programme evaluation; Bloom, Hastings and Madaus (1971) applied them to student learning, especially mastery learning.

concept: CBCS course types: AECC, SEC, DSE, GE
must_teach: UGC CBCS: Core, Discipline Specific Elective, Generic Elective, Ability Enhancement Compulsory Courses (Environmental Science, English/MIL Communication) and Skill Enhancement Courses (skill-based, chosen from a pool).
flag: DATED: uses 2015 UGC CBCS course categories (AECC/SEC/DSE/GE); CCFUP 2022 renamed/reshaped these (AEC, SEC, VAC, MDC) — guide should present both and note which framework the question assumes.

concept: Achievement goal theory: performance vs mastery goals
must_teach: Mastery (learning) goals aim to understand and improve; performance goals aim to demonstrate ability relative to others; work-avoidance aims at minimal effort.

concept: Teaching vs instruction
must_teach: Instruction is organised imparting of knowledge and can be done by a book, programme or machine; teaching in the strict sense involves a person interacting with the learner. All teaching includes instruction, not all instruction is teaching.

concept: Split-half reliability inflated for speed tests
must_teach: Split-half (odd-even) gives spuriously high reliability on speed tests because halves are nearly identical; test-retest or parallel forms should be used for speeded tests. Power tests can use split-half.

concept: Kolb's four learning styles and their mode pairs
must_teach: Diverger: concrete experience + reflective observation; assimilator: abstract conceptualisation + reflective observation; converger: abstract conceptualisation + active experimentation; accommodator: concrete experience + active experimentation.

concept: Motivation at memory (extrinsic) and reflective (intrinsic) levels
must_teach: At memory level motivation is mostly extrinsic (marks, praise, reproof); at reflective level it is mostly intrinsic, from the learner's felt problem.

concept: Enabling vs terminal objectives; Eisner's expressive objectives
must_teach: Terminal objective: what the learner can do at the end. Enabling objectives: intermediate component skills found by task analysis. Expressive objectives (Eisner) describe an encounter without specifying outcome.

concept: Ausubel's progressive differentiation vs integrative reconciliation
must_teach: Progressive differentiation: present most general, inclusive ideas first, then detail. Integrative reconciliation: explicitly relate new ideas to earlier ones and resolve contradictions.

concept: Halo effect vs leniency and central tendency errors
must_teach: Halo effect: favourable impression on one trait spreads to rating of unrelated traits. Leniency error: rating everyone high. Central tendency error: rating everyone near the middle.

concept: Creative Commons licence elements BY, SA, NC, ND
must_teach: BY = attribution required; SA = share-alike (adaptations under same licence); NC = non-commercial; ND = no derivatives. Open licences remove the need for individual permission.

concept: Forum: audience participation after lecture under a chairperson
must_teach: A forum is open discussion where the whole audience asks questions and comments, usually after a lecture, panel or symposium. In panel discussion and symposium, a few selected persons on the platform do the main talking.

concept: Andragogy, heutagogy and the PAH continuum
must_teach: Andragogy involves learners in diagnosing needs; heutagogy (Hase and Kenyon) emphasises capability and double-loop learning with the learner determining the path; pedagogy-andragogy-heutagogy form a continuum of increasing autonomy.

concept: UGC SWAYAM credit transfer regulations
must_teach: UGC (Credit Framework for Online Learning Courses through SWAYAM) Regulations allow institutions to accept SWAYAM courses up to a ceiling per semester and give equivalent credit.
flag: DATED: credit-transfer ceiling (20%/40%) depends on UGC regulations version (2016, 2021) — guide should give the current limit with date.

concept: Fixed cut-off is criterion-referenced; top percentage is norm-referenced
must_teach: A fixed minimum score that any number can meet is criterion-referenced; selection by rank (top x per cent) is norm-referenced; selection tests often combine both.

concept: Formal operational thought is abstract and hypothetical
must_teach: Piaget's formal operational stage frees thought from the concrete: reasoning about propositions, possibilities and hypotheses. Dependence on concrete objects marks the concrete operational stage.

concept: Elaborative vs maintenance rehearsal (Craik and Lockhart)
must_teach: Maintenance rehearsal is plain repetition to hold items in short-term memory; elaborative rehearsal links items to existing knowledge (deep processing, Craik and Lockhart) and aids long-term retention.

concept: Chunking overcomes limited working memory capacity (Miller 7 plus/minus 2)
must_teach: Miller: short-term/working memory holds about seven plus or minus two items; chunking groups items into meaningful units to stay within capacity. Interference explains forgetting; the sensory register is brief.

concept: Mayer's coherence and modality principles of multimedia design
must_teach: Mayer's coherence principle: extraneous material, even attractive, reduces learning. Modality principle: graphics are better with spoken narration than on-screen text.

concept: Gagné's events paired with internal learning processes
must_teach: Gaining attention supports reception; informing objective creates expectancy; learning guidance supports semantic encoding; feedback provides reinforcement.

concept: CAI modes: tutorial, drill-and-practice, simulation; branching resemblance
must_teach: Tutorial mode teaches new material through dialogue and, with remedial routing, resembles Crowder's branching programming. Drill and practice rehearses taught material; simulation models a real system.

concept: Piaget's egocentric speech vs Vygotsky's private speech
must_teach: Piaget saw children's self-talk as egocentric speech showing immaturity that fades; Vygotsky saw it as private speech that guides and regulates thought and later becomes inner speech.

concept: Performance assessment: validity gain, reliability and practicability loss
must_teach: Replacing written tests with observed performance raises validity (direct evidence) but lowers reliability (small sample, observer variation) and practicability (time); rubrics and multiple observations limit the loss.

concept: Cyclic relation of pre-active, interactive and post-active phases
must_teach: Post-active reflection can lead to action research; interactive decisions are steered by learners' verbal and non-verbal feedback; post-active evaluation feeds the next pre-active plan; experience shortens but does not remove planning.

concept: Locating an objective in the revised taxonomy table
must_teach: Taxonomy table: verb gives cognitive process, noun gives knowledge dimension (factual, conceptual, procedural, metacognitive). Judging one's own study strategies = Evaluate x metacognitive knowledge.

concept: Concept attainment model syntax and information-processing family
must_teach: Concept attainment (Bruner) phases: presentation of examples and non-examples, testing attainment, analysis of thinking strategies; it is in the information-processing family, as are inquiry training and advance organiser.

concept: Steps in constructing an achievement test
must_teach: Order: planning with blueprint, writing items, try-out on a sample, item analysis, assembling the final form.

concept: Keller's ARCS model of motivation
must_teach: ARCS: Attention (e.g. puzzling case), Relevance (link to goals), Confidence (graded tasks with early success), Satisfaction (rewards, use of learning).

concept: Features of problem-based learning
must_teach: PBL presents an ill-structured problem before content is taught; the tutor acts as facilitator; a physical product is characteristic of the project method, not PBL.

concept: Converting raw score to z and T-score
Morrison's mastery formula: teach, test, re-teach until mastery
must_teach: Morrison's mastery test ends assimilation; pupils who fall short of the mastery standard return to supervised study with corrective help and are re-tested before organisation and recitation.

concept: Lecture lacks feedback from receivers in communication terms
must_teach: In communication terms a lecture has sender, message, channel and receivers, but largely lacks feedback; questions, pauses and short tasks restore the feedback loop.

concept: Continued relevance of traditional aids in ICT classrooms
must_teach: Traditional aids (charts, models, chalkboard) remain useful: inexpensive, need no electricity, under teacher's control, models can be handled. Good teaching combines traditional and digital support.
